subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate with no noble house affiliation, no known lineage, and no apparent strategic value in Menzoberranzan, yet someone has paid a significant sum — described as 'they interrupt you, a lot' — to ensure his survival.
source_quote: You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a Drow mercenary from Menzoberranzan, part of a pair hired to protect Daz from House Mizzrym and House T'sarran; she exhibits professional detachment, understands the value of insulation in high-stakes contracts, and dismisses Daz’s self-mythologizing with cold pragmatism.
source_quote: That is a fee... that is a price you cannot afford.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is Nym’s sister and fellow mercenary; she displays acute professional confusion at the anomaly of Daz’s existence — a nobody worth massive investment — and her blunt assessments reveal a deep familiarity with the political calculus of Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: For all we know, this was a game being played by the houses.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a Lolth cleric who seized authority after a chaotic escape, displaying unwavering confidence in her divine favor; her actions provoked lethal intervention from Zalthir, who deemed her an immediate existential threat.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combat-trained individual with an Eldritch Claw Tattoo, trained in decisive action under moral uncertainty; he executed Asha Vandree without hesitation, believing someone had to make the call — and that he was the one who should.
source_quote: Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the party who attempted to subdue Asha Vandree via grapple, believing non-lethal restraint sufficient; his reluctance to kill reflects a moral code at odds with the lethal pragmatism of the Drow mercenaries.
source_quote: I don't like killing people if I don't have to.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric who opposes lethal force and seeks non-violent resolutions; he attempted divine intervention against Asha, but his failure led him to quietly reassess his role in the group’s decisions.
source_quote: Let's put a period after that 'now that I'm in charge' thing.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is one of the two noble houses in Menzoberranzan identified as a threat to Daz; the mercenaries were contracted to prevent them from killing him.
source_quote: House Mizzrym. House T'sarran. Those were the parameters.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is the second noble house identified as a threat to Daz; the mercenaries were prepared to handle them personally if necessary, but Daz eliminated their goons himself.
source_quote: We'd just finished burning. ... They'd been prepared to handle the T'sarran contingent personally if it came to that.

subject: Ilvara's House
fact: Ilvara's House is referenced as an additional threat to Daz, though not named explicitly as a noble house; the mercenaries were hired to protect him from them as well.
source_quote: Hired to protect me — specifically, me — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons...

subject: Lolth Cult (Asha's Affiliation)
fact: Asha Vandree’s devotion to Lolth is presented as genuine, though her interpretation of divine favor is dangerously delusional; her cultic authority is perceived as a lethal threat by Zalthir and the Drow mercenaries.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!

subject: T'sarran Goons
fact: T'sarran Goons are low-ranking enforcers of House T'sarran, recently eliminated by Daz and the party before the mercenaries arrived; their destruction demonstrated Daz’s capability and reduced the need for direct intervention.
source_quote: The T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Extraction Contract
fact: The extraction contract is a document produced by the party that appears central to the events leading to Daz’s targeting; it was scorched and referenced as evidence of the danger they escaped.
source_quote: Kaelira gestured toward the scorched remnants of the extraction contract the party had produced — the document that had apparently been at the center of all this...

subject: Hiring of Drow Mercenaries
fact: An anonymous, high-level patron in Menzoberranzan hired Nym and Kaelira to protect Daz, using cutouts to obscure their identity; the payment was substantial and unusual for a non-noble target.
source_quote: Someone had paid for this. Someone who knew I was here, knew who was hunting me, and knew enough to contract professionals rather than handle it directly.

subject: Execution of Asha Vandree
fact: Zalthir executed Asha Vandree with his Eldritch Claw Tattoo to prevent her from invoking Lolth’s power; the act ended a tense standoff and forced the party to confront the moral cost of survival in Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: The strikes came in sequence... Asha Vandree did not get another word out.

subject: Daz’s True Identity
fact: The mystery of why someone in Menzoberranzan invested so heavily in protecting Daz — a nobody with no house, no history, no value — is an unresolved plot thread; the answer may lie in hidden lineage, divine intervention, or a larger political game.
source_quote: So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?

subject: The Identity of the Paymaster
fact: The true identity of the patron who paid 'a lot' — enough to interrupt their schedule multiple times — remains unknown; the insulation around the transaction implies the payer fears exposure for reasons of illegality, embarrassment, or danger.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing: the payer has significant reason not to be associated with the purchase.

subject: The Meaning of the Three Bravos
fact: The three repeated 'bravos' from Kaelira after Daz’s actions signal professional irony — the third is never sincere — hinting that her praise masks suspicion, calculation, or hidden knowledge.
source_quote: Three *bravos*. I have found, as a general principle, that a third *bravo* is never sincere.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is the dominant drow city-state where noble houses wield power through violence, lineage, and ritual; its culture demands absolute loyalty to house structure, making Daz’s anonymity and high-value protection a profound anomaly.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing...

subject: The Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow is a reference to a training or philosophical tradition that taught Zalthir about social authority and power dynamics; it informs his perception of threats and his readiness to act decisively.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying — or possibly Brother Quellin did... that the most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn.

subject: After the Extraction
fact: The events occur immediately after the party’s escape from an extraction operation, which triggered the intervention of the Drow mercenaries and the subsequent confrontation with Asha Vandree.
source_quote: The T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: Since Velkynvelve
fact: Daz has been maintaining a mental list of threats and potential allies since the events at Velkynvelve, marking the beginning of his conscious awareness of being targeted.
source_quote: I'd been running a list in the back of my head since Velkynvelve...

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who became indistinguishable from Zuggtmoy's rot, and was looted with efficient respect after her theological problem was resolved.
source_quote: I looted her with the efficient respect one extends to a theological problem that has been resolved.

subject: Sealed wax pouch from Asha Vandree
fact: Contained a meticulously written theological treatise arguing that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity — a conclusion reached through backward reasoning, deemed both well-argued and completely mad.
source_quote: Inside were pages of close, careful script — the handwriting of someone who had once been methodical, who had trained as a theologian and brought that training to bear on a question that should not have been asked.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: A standard Lolth devotional text corrupted by marginalia in a second hand — documenting the slow, ambiguous subversion by Zuggtmoy, possibly written by Ilvara herself in a changed mental state.
source_quote: The marginalia told the story... Two hands because two minds had been working the same pen.

subject: Sealed orders from House Mizzrym
fact: Frustrated, escalating inquiries into Ilvara's disappearance — revealing that her faction had no awareness of her theological collapse until she was gone.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you?

subject: Letter from Neverlight Grove
fact: A missed political meeting — evidence that Ilvara’s allegiance had shifted beyond recovery, prioritizing Zuggtmoy’s influence over any earthly alliance.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: The Living Serpent Head Scourge
fact: A scourge with a head that was once a living serpent, now in an intermediate state between life and death — a remarkable artifact of terrible origin, to be documented, not endorsed.
source_quote: It sounds like a great museum piece... You document them. You label them carefully. You do not pretend they aren't what they are.

subject: Water-damaged prisoner journal
fact: A fragmented record kept by a prisoner who wrote until they could no longer — their handwriting faded but legible in dry sections, showing persistence until the end.
source_quote: The pages were swollen and the ink had run in places, but the handwriting was still visible in the drier sections, the marks of a person who had kept records right up until they couldn't.

subject: Flask of Overbright brandy
fact: Received with personal interest — an item of sensory and possibly magical significance, distinct from the theological and corporeal relics.
source_quote: The flask of Overbright brandy I received with considerably more personal interest.

subject: Ilvara
fact: A high priestess of Lolth whose theology was subverted by Zuggtmoy, evidenced by marginalia in her prayer book and her collection of prisoner trophies — including Thorin's tooth.
source_quote: She had been carrying his tooth around the Underdark. She had collected it like a curiosity.

subject: Thorin
fact: A prisoner whose tooth was taken as a trophy by Ilvara and later reclaimed — his quiet recognition of its significance revealing the personal cost of theological domination.
source_quote: Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back. He held it for a moment without saying anything. Then: 'Very sentimental.'

subject: Theological subversion of Ilvara
fact: A slow, ambiguous corruption by Zuggtmoy, documented in marginalia and behavior, leaving uncertainty whether Ilvara knew she was losing herself — a case study in invisible subversion.
source_quote: I could not tell from the text whether she had known she wasn't resisting or whether she had genuinely believed she was still moving in her own direction.

subject: The origin of the theological treatise
fact: The author of the wax pouch treatise remains unknown — but their mind was shaped by centuries of Lolthite theological contortion, now twisted into a new, heretical unity with Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: Clerics of Lolth have been doing this kind of theological contortion for centuries; what was unusual here was the destination.

subject: The second hand in Ilvara's prayer book
fact: The marginalia may have been written by an external influence — or by Ilvara herself in a fractured state — raising the question of agency in theological corruption.
source_quote: Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Discovery of Ilvara's corruption timeline
fact: The prayer book's marginalia revealed a gradual, non-linear descent into Zuggtmoy's influence — a process that began subtly and was never consciously resisted.
source_quote: The early entries were neat and formal... Then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in.

subject: Looting of Asha Vandree's remains
fact: The efficient looting of Asha Vandree’s body marked the closure of a theological anomaly — her identity as a cleric of two incompatible deities resolved through death.
source_quote: I looted her with the efficient respect one extends to a theological problem that has been resolved.

subject: Drow Outpost
fact: A site of theological decay — where prisoner belongings, prayer books, and treatises reveal the collapse of drow religious hierarchy under Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: A cleric's catalogue of the things a high priestess of Lolth becomes when something older and stranger finds the seam in her theology and begins to work.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: A drow house unaware of Ilvara’s subversion — their frantic communications reveal a political structure blind to internal theological collapse.
source_quote: House Mizzrym would learn eventually, I supposed. We had helped with that.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: A political entity whose alliance with Ilvara dissolved without notice — evidence that Zuggtmoy’s influence overrode even formal diplomatic ties.
source_quote: Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: The merchant Tongued by a bardic curse
fact: A past case of linguistic and psychological fragmentation — eerily similar to Ilvara’s marginalia — suggesting a pattern of external corruption manifesting as textual dissonance.
source_quote: I had seen something like this before, in a completely different context — a merchant I once knew who had been Tongued by a bardic curse...

subject: Collection of prisoner trophies by Ilvara
fact: Ilvara kept personal items from prisoners — including Thorin’s tooth — as relics of ownership, demonstrating the dehumanizing theology of Lolth fused with Zuggtmoy’s possessive rot.
source_quote: She had been carrying his tooth around the Underdark. She had collected it like a curiosity.

subject: The meaning of 'Very sentimental'
fact: Thorin’s quiet acceptance of his tooth’s return — and his use of the phrase — hints at a deeper emotional wound, one that survived theological and physical domination.
source_quote: He held it for a moment without saying anything. Then: 'Very sentimental.'

subject: Chain mail, prayer beads, and holy symbol of Lolth from Asha Vandree
fact: Standard clerical gear from a cleric who had become a vessel for rot — items now separated from their sacred context, reduced to loot.
source_quote: The holy symbol of Lolth. Chain mail. Prayer beads. And a sealed wax pouch.

subject: Drow cloak of spider-silk from Asha Vandree
fact: A fine, shadow-absorbing garment taken by Zalthir — a relic of drow elegance now stripped of its wearer’s identity.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow — and I did not begrudge him that.

subject: The silence after 'Is this pre-craziness or post-craziness?'
fact: No one could answer — the distinction between theological corruption and madness had become indistinguishable, and the group had no framework to classify it.
source_quote: Is this pre-craziness or post-craziness, do you think?" I asked. No one answered with any certainty.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend recovered a necromantic pearl from the core of Ilvara's corrupted fungal ritual site and reclaimed his stolen tooth, marking the beginning and escalation of the corruption he and his party endured at Velkynvelve.
source_quote: Two objects. One that marked where we started, and one that marked how far the corruption had spread by the time we got here.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan, is the target of a high-cost contract orchestrated by House T'sarran, yet has no knowledge of why he is valued enough to warrant such attention.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence... And yet.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym, one of the Duskryn sisters, is sharply skeptical of Daz’s possible noble lineage, interpreting his mysterious value as typical orphan fantasy, and expresses irritation with the lack of clarity in their contract.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery... For all we know, this was a game being played by the houses.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira, the other Duskryn sister, is professionally detached and methodical, prioritizing factual analysis over speculation, and offers the most honest assessment of their mission’s limitations.
source_quote: Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend possesses deep familiarity with Dawnbringer’s personality and maintains a stable, repetitive dynamic with the sentient sunblade, using the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard as a diplomatic tool.
source_quote: Do I need to show you the scabbard again?

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade with strong opinions against being used as a ritual object, insisting on its identity as a weapon of destruction rather than purification.
source_quote: I'm not some kind of magical wizard thingy that purifies things. I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara, a former High Priestess, used a fungal mass as a ritual anchor to merge the symbols of Zuggtmoy and Lolth, creating a corrupted nexus that produced a necromantic pearl, before being slain by Grygum.
source_quote: Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a decisive and ruthless agent of purification, using acid to eradicate fungal corruption tied to Zuggtmoy, showing no tolerance for lingering necromantic influence.
source_quote: He opened his mouth, and the acid came out clean and decisive, and the fungal matter... collapsed into ash in the time it takes to exhale.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran contracted professional Drow mercenaries to extract Daz alive and unharmed, indicating significant resources and reach behind the operation.
source_quote: There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym deployed soldiers to the chamber where Ilvara conducted her rituals; their corpses were found with weapons and insignia, suggesting they were part of a failed enforcement or guard detail.
source_quote: The dead soldiers of House Mizzrym would never collect their pay.

subject: Necromantic Pearl
fact: A fist-sized, dense, smooth object found at the core of Ilvara’s fungal ritual site, radiating unnatural stillness and necromantic energy, unlike anything grown naturally.
source_quote: Smooth. Dense. Fist-sized. The weight of it was wrong for something grown — too even, too finished, like a stone that had been worked by a hand that knew what it was doing.

subject: Ilvara's Tooth
fact: A chip of Thorin’s tooth, taken as a trophy by Ilvara during his capture at Velkynvelve and later reclaimed, symbolizing the personal violation and the closure of a debt.
source_quote: She'd taken my tooth. A chip broken off in the capture, displayed in her chest like a piece of evidence of what she could do.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: A sentient sunblade with strong aversion to being used in ritual purification, asserting its identity as a weapon of destruction, and responsive to the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard’s authority.
source_quote: I'm not some kind of magical wizard thingy that purifies things. I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things.

subject: T'sarran Signet Ring
fact: The signet ring of House T'sarran found on the corpse of the mage who carried the contract to extract Daz, serving as physical proof of the house’s involvement.
source_quote: I found the signet ring first — House T'sarran, the seal unmistakable on the face of it.

subject: Obsidian Wand with Captive Spider
fact: An obsidian wand containing a preserved spider in amber, recovered from the mage’s remains, suggesting arcane use tied to entrapment or control.
source_quote: Then the wand: obsidian, a captive spider preserved in amber at its tip.

subject: Cloth with Lolth-Zuggtmoy Sigil
fact: A stitched cloth bearing the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy’s mark interwoven with Lolth’s web, symbolizing Ilvara’s blasphemous fusion of two deities and her ritual corruption.
source_quote: A cloth that had been stitched with two sigils — Lolth's web worked into the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy's mark, one woven inside the other.

subject: Contract to Extract Daz
fact: A high-value, multi-layered contract orchestrated by House T'sarran to extract Daz alive and unharmed, involving professional Drow mercenaries and significant financial expenditure.
source_quote: Someone had spent a significant amount of gold to ensure that the elf standing to my left made it out of this cavern breathing.

subject: Purification Attempt with Dawnbringer
fact: A proposed ritual purification using Dawnbringer was rejected by the blade, leading to a negotiated compromise facilitated by Thorin’s use of the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard.
source_quote: I suppose… I could do you this one. I could do this solid for you.

subject: Eradication of Zuggtmoy's Fungal Corruption
fact: Grygum destroyed the fungal growth tied to Zuggtmoy’s influence with acid, reducing it to ash and eliminating the last vestiges of Ilvara’s ritual anchor.
source_quote: The fungal matter that had spent months becoming something wrong collapsed into ash in the time it takes to exhale.

subject: Daz's True Identity
fact: The origin of the contract targeting Daz remains unresolved, creating a persistent mystery about whether he is a lost noble, a hidden asset, or a pawn in a larger game.
source_quote: So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?

subject: The Necromantic Pearl's Origin
fact: The source of the necromantic pearl — whether grown under specific conditions or placed deliberately — is unknown, representing a deeper mystery tied to Ilvara’s rituals and the chamber’s corruption.
source_quote: A rock in the wrong place is just a rock. A rock in the right place is a wall. The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident.

subject: The Burning Documents
fact: Partially burned documents recovered from the mage’s remains confirm the contract but lack full context, leaving gaps in understanding the motives, intermediaries, and ultimate goals behind Daz’s extraction.
source_quote: They'd been partially burned, which meant someone had tried to destroy them and hadn't quite managed it.

subject: Chamber of Ilvara's Ritual
fact: A corrupted chamber where Ilvara fused the symbols of Zuggtmoy and Lolth into a fungal ritual nexus, producing the necromantic pearl and attracting House T'sarran’s interest.
source_quote: The fungal mass sat at the center of the chamber the way a problem sits at the center of a bad situation — obvious, unavoidable, radiating something wrong in every direction.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: The prison where Daz and Thorin were held, and where Ilvara first took Thorin’s tooth as a trophy, marking the beginning of their entanglement with her corruption.
source_quote: When we'd first found ourselves hanging in nets at Velkynvelve, Ilvara had made a point of collecting trophies.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events described occurred during the current expedition following the party’s escape from Velkynvelve, with no explicit calendar date provided.
source_quote: I had the necromantic pearl in one pocket. I'd already turned over the question of what it meant... We still had a chamber to clear.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is contemplating a sword whisperer to address the spiritual wear of Dawnbringer after months in the Underdark, and refuses to relinquish the blade, treating it as an extension of his identity.
source_quote: Thorin stood with his face at an angle that suggested he was calculating the sun's position relative to the year.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum experienced a genuine spiritual moment in direct sunlight and has accumulated a list of pamphlets and lore he intends to pursue at Candlekeep, particularly regarding Bahamut, treating the library as both research site and pilgrimage.
source_quote: Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the de facto architect of the group's next steps, steering the decision toward Candlekeep to research House T'sarran, Jimjar's disappearance, and his own history, while already drafting journal entries and analyzing everything before fully arriving.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the gelatinous ward transformed into a grey ooze, reacted to the Overbright not with fear but with wide, attentive curiosity — his first exposure to sunlight producing a silent, childlike wonder that surpassed the group's own reactions.
source_quote: He peered. He had not been in sunlight before. ... He took it in the way a child takes in a first ocean.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz possesses the Stonespeaker Crystal and has documented Glabbagool's reaction to the surface world, filing it as data among other observations relevant to his own mysterious past.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's. But I noted the response. Filed it.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is the target of research at Candlekeep, linked to Jimjar's disappearance and the activities of hired Duskryns, suggesting a hidden conspiracy tied to Daz's origins.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: Duskryns
fact: Hired Duskryns are acting as cutouts or intermediaries in a shadow network pointing toward Daz's past, their purpose unclear but their trail significant enough to warrant investigation.
source_quote: whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: emergence into the Overbright
fact: The group emerged from the Underdark into the Overbright, a phenomenon of all-encompassing, non-sourced light that caused profound physiological and psychological shifts in every member, including Glabbagool and the Drow-cloaked crew.
source_quote: The light that came through the tunnel mouth was not like Dawnbringer's light... It was a light that simply *was*, filling everything from every direction at once.

subject: opening of the bag of holding
fact: Grygum opened the bag of holding, allowing Glabbagool to emerge into sunlight for the first time, triggering an unprecedented reaction of curiosity in the ooze and revealing a vulnerability in the group’s logistics.
source_quote: Grygum had opened the bag of holding just enough, and Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward... had peered out.

subject: decision to pursue gear over investment
fact: The group agreed to spend surplus gold on adventuring gear rather than business ventures, recognizing their instability and the likelihood of continued danger from the demon lord situation.
source_quote: We agreed on the gear.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep, the Great Library, is the chosen destination for research into House T'sarran, Jimjar's disappearance, Daz's history, and Bahamutian lore, serving as both intellectual hub and spiritual sanctuary for the group.
source_quote: Candlekeep, the Great Library, research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance...

subject: The Overbright
fact: The Overbright is the surface world’s radiant, non-sourced light — a phenomenon that fundamentally alters perception, triggers spiritual awakening, and exposes the group to vulnerabilities (e.g., Drow cloaks disintegrating) they were unprepared for.
source_quote: The Overbright was a concept I had been carrying... It was a light that simply *was*, filling everything from every direction at once.

subject: Drow cloaks
fact: Drow cloaks disintegrate upon exposure to sunlight, a known material impermanence taught in monastic curricula, which the group had prepared for by storing them in a bag.
source_quote: I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight.

subject: Bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding was used to transport Glabbagool safely through the Underdark, but its accidental opening exposed the ooze to sunlight for the first time, triggering a transformative reaction.
source_quote: Grygum had opened the bag of holding just enough, and Glabbagool... had peered out.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient blade forged for radiance, now worn by Thorin after enduring months of darkness in the Underdark, and is the subject of a quest to find a sword whisperer to restore its spiritual integrity.
source_quote: Thorin, characteristically, was thinking about Dawnbringer... months of darkness, months of the deep, a blade whose nature was radiance forced to endure the complete absence of the thing it was built to carry.

subject: Stonespeaker Crystal
fact: The Stonespeaker Crystal is held by Daz and has been used to record and analyze Glabbagool’s reaction to the surface world, serving as a tool for archiving the group’s evolving understanding of the Overbright’s impact.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's. But I noted the response. Filed it.

subject: Daz's hidden history
fact: A mystery surrounds Daz’s origins, hinted at by the actions of Duskryns and the obscurity of House T'sarran, and is the central unresolved thread driving the group’s journey to Candlekeep.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: Glabbagool's sentience
fact: Glabbagool’s reaction to the Overbright suggests a depth of awareness and emotional response previously unobserved in gelatinous creatures, raising the question of whether he is merely a ward or something more — a sentient being shaped by the Underdark.
source_quote: He took it in the way a child takes in a first ocean, the way the sheer scale of a thing produces a silence that is not quite awe but is adjacent to it.

subject: the sword whisperer
fact: Thorin believes a specialist — a 'sword whisperer' — exists who can restore Dawnbringer’s spiritual resonance after its prolonged exposure to darkness, though no such figure has been confirmed, making this a speculative quest.
source_quote: The phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about.

subject: elapsed time in the Underdark
fact: The group spent an indeterminate number of months in the Underdark — so long that even the narrator cannot recall the duration — during which they endured darkness, isolation, and transformation.
source_quote: I genuinely cannot tell you how many months it had been.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, once a gelatinous ward of the Underdark, is now a grey ooze who survived the bag of holding, the ooze crisis, and months of travel — his first encounter with sunlight revealing curiosity rather than instinctive retreat.
source_quote: Glabbagool had survived Blingdenstone, the ooze crisis, the bag of holding, and however many months of Underdark travel, and his first reaction to the surface world was curiosity rather than retreat.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth is a surviving member of the group who emerged into the Overbright alongside the others, though her specific actions and reactions remain unrecorded beyond her presence in the cohort.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait is a surviving member of the group who emerged into the Overbright, noted only as part of the collective, with no individual actions or reactions described.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.
